kernel_pls Semantic Regression vs Vanilla Neural Retrieval

Comparison of embedding-based regression against direct neural feature nearest-neighbor matching

Executive Summary

Word Accuracy

12/12

Vanilla wins (out of 12 patients)

Wilcoxon p = 0.0005 (two-sided)

Category Accuracy

9/12

Vanilla wins (out of 12 patients)

Wilcoxon p = 0.1763 (two-sided)

Methods

Vanilla retrieval: Leave-one-out nearest-centroid matching in raw neural feature space (high-gamma 70–150 Hz, no embedding projection, no regression model).

kernel_pls semantic regression: Mapping neural features to semantic embedding space (GloVe, FastText, Word2Vec, ConceptNet, DINOv2, SimCLR); cosine similarity retrieval.

Significance: Paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test across 12 patients at each metric's peak time bin.

Interpretation

Vanilla strength: Direct neural feature matching has no bottleneck of embedding space projection; may capture patient-specific neural signatures that don't align with generic word embeddings.

kernel_pls potential advantage: Embedding-based approaches can generalize across semantic relationships and leverage pre-trained semantic knowledge.

Time dynamics: Peaks may differ between methods due to different feature spaces and regularization. Vanilla peaks on raw neural features; kernel_pls peaks in embedding space after regression.

Patient heterogeneity: Some patients (e.g., RB, CP per CLAUDE.md) may have more visual-area coverage, favoring image embeddings or direct neural matches. Individual electrode locations matter.
